query: interfaces in src that a For each synchronized detection and depth pair, send stage 2 only the pallet select_detection already chooses, and write both sides of that split onto the result the handling process reads. PalletPoseStamped gains the chosen candidate's source index as the pallet sent through stage 2, and the source indices of the other class-matched candidates in that same Detection2DArray as deferred. Those indices are the slots extract_detection_candidates already stored. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the roster is this capture while the scene can still change. When the estimate fails, the same two lists go on the failure diagnostic, which is the only result that path publishes. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. Stage 2 still runs once. The user named which detections are sent versus deferred; the part they did not name is that both lists sit on PalletPoseStamped, the pose result for the AGV controller, rather than only on a diagnostic the success path does not use. change must keep working
findings: The success result in src is pps_perception_msgs/PalletPoseStamped on pallet_pose_topic (default and pallet_pose_cpp.yaml /pps/pallet_pose_rich, publisher depth 10). eval_recorder_node is the only subscriber. It joins format_stamp(input_rgb_stamp) to stamp_map.json and copies yaw_rad, pose.position, n_face_points, plane_inlier_ratio, and chamfer_cost_m. It skips every DiagnosticStatus whose level is not WARN, so the success-path OK diagnostic is unread. The message comment names this rich pose as the AGV controller result. geometry_msgs/PoseStamped on pose_topic (yaml and mock pipeline /pps/pallet_pose) stays a header plus a pose: test_full_pipeline_launch.py requires a finite pose with tz in (1.5, 2.5) and |tx| and |ty| under 0.20 m. dataset_replay.launch maps its pose_topic argument (default /pps/pallet_pose_rich) onto pallet_pose_topic and the recorder, and leaves the node's pose_topic parameter on the yaml PoseStamped name.

Existing PalletPoseStamped fields stay in place and stay filled on the success publish: header.stamp is the node clock and header.frame_id is the detection frame or camera_rgb_optical_frame; pose is the optical-frame yaw quaternion; yaw_rad, face_normal_rgb, plane_inlier_ratio, n_face_points, chamfer_cost_m (0 when has_debug is false), accepted true, failure_reason empty, geometry_source, preset_id geometry_core_default, input_rgb_stamp, and input_depth_stamp. quality_reasons stays the default empty array. An int32 for the chosen source_index and an int32[] for the other stored source_index values append after input_depth_stamp. int32[] is an unbounded sequence, and field names stay lowercase. A zero sent index is a real detections slot. An empty deferred sequence is the one-candidate case. The four srv files generated beside this msg do not reference it.

DetectionCandidate.source_index is the index in vision_msgs/Detection2DArray.detections. extract_detection_candidates skips an empty results list and a target_class_id mismatch and does not renumber, which test_detection_utils locks (empty results yield no candidate; a forklift at slot 0 leaves the pallet at source_index 1). The class compared is the highest-scoring ObjectHypothesis.class_id string. The detector writes class_label (pallet), not the numeric pallet_class_id, into that string, copies the RGB Image header onto the array, leaves Detection2D.id empty, and publishes score-descending boxes capped by max_detections (default 10). Detection2D.id is the optional cross-message id and may be empty. The roster slots are those stored source_index values for this array.

select_detection stays highest_confidence (score, then area_px) and largest_area (area_px, then score), returns nullopt on an empty list, and throws std::invalid_argument on an unknown strategy. std::max_element keeps the first maximum, so a tie stays with the earlier source_index. Tests lock the winner at source_index 1 for both strategies. on_pair calls estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 once, with that bbox and that source_index as instance_id. PoseResult.instance_id and FailureResult.instance_id hold that optional int and are not a published field today. The deferred list is the other source_index values in that same candidate vector. eval_recorder select_best_detection mirrors the same filter and strategy for the bbox and does not store source_index. target_class_id pallet and detection_selection highest_confidence stay aligned in pallet_pose_cpp.yaml, pipeline_nodes.py, and dataset_replay.launch.py.

The pair interface is message_filters ApproximateTime of sensor_msgs/Image and Detection2DArray, queue sync_queue_size 10, setMaxIntervalDuration from sync_slop_s (default 0.10 s). Topics stay the parameters (yaml depth /camera/depth/image_rect, detections /pps/detections). input_rgb_stamp is det_msg->header.stamp. input_depth_stamp is depth_msg->header.stamp. PalletPoseStamped carries them as builtin_interfaces/Time, whose nanosec is in [0, 1e9). Diagnostics carry stamp_to_string, seconds, a dot, and nanosec zero-padded to 9, the same text as build_bag.format_stamp. DiagnosticArray.header.stamp and both pose headers stay publish time. The Image header timestamp should be the acquisition time, and Detection2D says the source pixels are not in the message and the header should match that source, recovered with an approximate synchronizer. The two capture stamps can differ inside the slop. The roster is this pair.

A stage-2 failure publishes one diagnostic_msgs/DiagnosticArray and returns. That is the only result on that path. The status stays name pps_pallet_pose_cpp, hardware_id dynamic_handling_ros_v1, level WARN (1), message equal to failure_reason, with KeyValues failure_reason, input_rgb_stamp, and input_depth_stamp. KeyValue is a string key and a string value. The recorder's dict keeps the last value for a repeated key, joins on input_rgb_stamp, and stores failure_reason or else status.message. A later WARN with the same stamp replaces that diag. _build_record uses the rich pose whenever it arrived, so a PalletPoseStamped on the failure path would take the success branch. The two lists are two new keys on this same WARN, and they leave failure_reason, input_rgb_stamp, and input_depth_stamp in place. The success OK status stays message pose_estimated with chamfer_cost_m, plane_inlier_ratio, n_face_points, and both stamps.

The two early returns stay unpublished. An empty candidate list returns before depth conversion and before stage 2. depth_image_to_meters throws std::invalid_argument on an unsupported encoding or a short buffer, and that path only logs. The recorder marks a sample with neither a rich pose nor a WARN diagnostic as no_response, and a WARN as failed. A diagnostic on either early return would record a failure for a pair that currently records no_response.

mock pipeline_nodes sets pose_topic and pallet_pose_topic and omits diagnostics_topic, so the C++ default /pps/pallet_pose_diagnostics must stay that name. Publishers use depth 10, which is keep-last on rmw_qos_profile_default: reliable and volatile. The recorder subscription is reliable, volatile, depth 50. A best-effort publisher would not match that subscription. Keep-last drops whole messages, so one PalletPoseStamped carries both lists and both capture stamps, and the failure path carries both lists on its one WARN.
